tapeLine: Friday 20 November: S&P 500 −3.7% to 6,910.39, a seventh straight loss, closing in correction more than 10% below its 6 Oct record; Nasdaq Composite −5.28% to 22,617.73, negative for 2026; Dow −949.73 (−1.93%) to 48,147.33. Weekly: S&P 500 −8.6%, Nasdaq about −10% (UPI; StockTitan; Stockinvest.us, 20 Nov). Sources differ slightly on the Dow’s figures.
matters:
Friday turned last week’s slide into a correction: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq Composite 5.3%, with the Nasdaq-100 briefly in bear-market territory intraday (UPI; StockTitan, 20 Nov). Chips led: Nvidia −14.01% to $125.53 after a Reuters report of an SEC accounting probe, with AMD and Broadcom down more than 13% (Motley Fool; Global Banking & Finance, 20 Nov). Reuters noted investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. Anthropic (ANT) fell 8.5% to $88.91 on its second day, touching $83.05, five cents above its $83 IPO price (CNN; AI Stock Wire, 20 Nov).

Early Monday, US futures were bouncing: S&P 500 futures up roughly 2.2–2.8% and Nasdaq-100 futures roughly 2.9–3.6% depending on the snapshot (Canadian Press via CP24; TipRanks; ABC Australia, 23 Nov). It is a holiday-shortened week: markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1:00 p.m. ET Friday, with October PCE and Q3 GDP second estimate on Wednesday (CP24; heygotrade, 23 Nov).

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield 4.92% Friday on the Treasury par curve (via EconLearn), 4.912% close per Investing.com, against about 5.06% Thursday; 2-year 4.63% (20 Nov). CNBC described the move as a flight to safety. Dollar, oil and gold Friday levels not confirmed and left out.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Friday 20 November: S&P 500 6,910.39 (−3.7%); Nasdaq Composite 22,617.73 (−5.28%); Dow 48,147.33 (−949.73, −1.93%) (UPI; StockTitan, 20 Nov).

Nvidia — −14.01% to $125.53 from $145.98 after a Reuters report of an SEC accounting probe; chipmakers had their worst week since 2001 per one account (Motley Fool; Global Banking & Finance; Zentrix, 20 Nov).
Anthropic (ANT) — −8.5% to $88.91 on day two, range $83.05–$92.56, volume about 400M shares vs 857M on debut; after-hours $87.80 (CNN; StockAnalysis; FinanceFeeds; heygotrade, 20 Nov).

Futures and abroad — early Monday 23 Nov: S&P 500 futures +2.2% to +2.8%, Nasdaq-100 futures +2.9% to +3.6%, Dow futures +1.6% to +1.9%, depending on time; Asian markets mostly lower (CP24; TipRanks; ABC Australia, 23 Nov). European flash PMIs mixed: Germany manufacturing 55.0 vs 54.1 expected; France composite 46.2 vs 48.1 expected (FXStreet; Newsquawk, 23 Nov).
macro: University of Michigan sentiment, November final — 51.5, up from 48.0 in October and from a 51.0 preliminary, in line with a ~51.5 estimate. Year-ahead inflation expectations 3.7% from 4.7%; five-year 3.3% from 3.5% (Bloomberg; investingLive; Advisor Perspectives, 20 Nov).

Week ahead — Wednesday 25 Nov, 8:30 ET: October PCE price index and Q3 GDP second estimate; durable goods and jobless claims also Wednesday, Beige Book Wednesday. Dell reports Tuesday after the close (heygotrade; Thrive in Markets, 23 Nov).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: S&P 500 and Dow in correction after seven straight S&P losses and an 8.6% weekly drop, led by chips and AI names, into a holiday-shortened week.
regime.sizing: Whether Monday’s 2–3% futures bounce holds through the open is unresolved; analysts quoted by Tickmill said a bounce need not become a recovery.

secondOrder: Friday’s selling was uneven: the Dow fell less than half as much as the Nasdaq, and Treasury yields dropped about 14 basis points as equities sold off, a reversal of the rising-yield backdrop earlier in the month. Anthropic’s day-two low came within cents of its IPO price. Observations, not forecasts.

scorecard.text: The prior brief reported Nasdaq-100 futures down about 1–1.4% early Friday and left open whether that carried into the close. It did, and more: the Nasdaq Composite closed −5.28% and the S&P 500 −3.7% (UPI; StockTitan, 20 Nov).
The prior brief carried a 51.6 preliminary November Michigan sentiment reading (XTB). The preliminary was 51.0; the final came in at 51.5 (investingLive; Bloomberg, 20 Nov).
The prior brief listed the Michigan final at 10:00 ET Friday with consensus 51.0–52; it printed 51.5, inside that range (investingLive, 20 Nov).
The prior brief listed Philadelphia Fed President Paulson speaking Friday evening; no coverage of the remarks was found, so it is not graded.
